issues.description: Field de.tum.cit.ase.Farm.animals has conflicting types across the exercise artifacts. In the UML in problem_statement.md (line 17) the attribute is declared as List<Animal> ("animals: List<Animal>"). However, the textual requirement in Part 3 of problem_statement.md (lines 108-109) explicitly requires unique animals and instructs to realize the aggregation using a Set implemented with a HashSet ("The aggregation between Farm and Animal is realized using a `Set`, implemented using a `HashSet`"). The reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, lines 9-13) implements animals as a List<Animal> with new ArrayList<>(), which contradicts the textual instructions. This inconsistency leaves students uncertain whether to implement Farm.animals as a List (allowing duplicates) or as a Set/HashSet (preventing duplicates) and may cause grading/implementation mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type for Farm.animals consistent across the UML, textual specification, template, and solution. Two concrete options: (A) Follow the textual requirement (preferred for uniqueness): update the UML in problem_statement.md to show animals: Set<Animal>, update the template and solution Farm.java to declare private Set<Animal> animals; import java.util.Set and java.util.HashSet; initialize animals = new HashSet<>(); change the getter/setter signatures to return/accept Set<Animal>; and keep addAnimal/add iteration logic working with Set. (B) Alternatively, if duplicates are acceptable, update the textual Part 3 to remove the Set/HashSet requirement and state that a List/ArrayList is used, and update the UML to animals: List<Animal>. Concretely for option A, replace in Farm.java: "private List<Animal> animals;" -> "private Set<Animal> animals;"; replace "this.animals = new ArrayList<>();" -> "this.animals = new HashSet<>();"; update imports and getter/setter types accordingly; and update the UML block in problem_statement.md to "animals: Set<Animal>". Ensure tests and wording reflect the chosen variant.
